nodes.name: Products
nodes.summary: Product list, creation, the product editor, variants, media and the availability diagnostics, with the GraphQL documents they send.
nodes.detail: Everything under src/products. The router maps /products to the list, /products/:id to the editor, and variant, media and variant-create pages under it. Views own data loading: each calls generated Apollo hooks built from products/queries.ts and products/mutations.ts, then hands data and callbacks to presentational page components. Edits on the product page are staged in one form and saved in a fixed sequence of mutations (files, product, channel listings, variant deletes, creates and updates). Creation is deliberately minimal: a dialog asks for a name and product type, and the rest is finished on the product page through a setup checklist.

nodes.name: Product list and creation
nodes.summary: The product list page in grid or tile view, its filters and export, and the dialog that creates a product.
nodes.detail: ProductList is the data view: it reads filters from the address bar, runs the ProductList query with cursor pagination and renders ProductListPage, which switches between a Glide datagrid and a tile grid by a value kept in local storage. Bulk delete and export run from here. The create dialog collects a name and product type, and createMinimalProduct turns that into one or two mutations before navigating to the editor with the setup checklist open.

nodes.name: Products router
nodes.summary: Maps the /products routes to the list, editor, variant, variant-create and media views, and redirects the legacy add route to the create dialog.
nodes.detail: Parses query strings into typed parameters for each view (sorting, array filters, dialog actions). /products/add no longer has a page: it redirects to the list with action=create-product and an optional product type. An old variant path is redirected to the current one, marked for removal in a later release.

nodes.name: Product list view
nodes.summary: Loads the product page of results for the current filters, channel and sort, and wires bulk delete, export and the create dialog.
nodes.detail: Builds query variables from the conditional filter container and the search text, then runs useProductListQuery with includeCategories and includeCollections only when those columns are visible. Attribute columns are loaded with a second GridAttributes query for the ids chosen in the column picker. Creating a product calls createMinimalProduct with three mutation callbacks, marks the onboarding step create-product as done and opens the new product with action=setup.

nodes.name: createMinimalProduct()
nodes.summary: Creates a product from a name and type; for types without variants it also creates one bare default variant and deletes the product if that fails.
nodes.detail: Sends productCreate with only name and productType. When the type has variants the work stops there. Otherwise it sends productVariantCreate with no attributes and the product name, so the detail page has a variant to take price and stock. If the variant create returns errors the product is deleted again, so the shop never keeps a simple product without a variant. Channel listings, category and search engine optimization (SEO) fields are left for the product page checklist.
nodes.signature: export const createMinimalProduct = async ({ name, productTypeId, hasVariants, productCreate, productVariantCreate, productDelete }) => Promise<CreateMinimalProductResult>

nodes.name: Create product dialog
nodes.summary: Modal that searches product types with a 500 millisecond debounce and asks for a product name, or offers to create a product type first.

nodes.name: Product list page
nodes.summary: Page shell with filters, view switch, bulk actions and either the datagrid or the tile list, chosen by the productListViewType local storage key.

nodes.name: Product list datagrid
nodes.summary: Glide datagrid of products with static and attribute columns, price and availability cells per channel, and row selection for bulk actions.

nodes.name: Product list filters
nodes.summary: Converts the conditional filter container and legacy query parameters into ProductFilterInput or where input, and stores saved filter presets.
nodes.detail: getFilterVariables reads the shared conditional filter container (owned by the shell) and returns either the legacy filter shape or the newer where shape; storageUtils keeps saved presets in local storage under the products filter key.

nodes.name: Product export parameters
nodes.summary: Builds the exportProducts input from the export dialog: scope (all, filtered or selected), file type, chosen fields and the active filters.

nodes.name: Product editor and save sequence
nodes.summary: The product detail page: one form for details, attributes, organization, channels and variants, saved by a handler that sends mutations in a fixed order.
nodes.detail: ProductUpdate loads the product with useProductDetailsQuery and its variants page by page with useProductVariantsGrid, then renders ProductUpdatePage inside ProductUpdateForm. The form tracks dirty fields, channel listing drafts and staged variant edits; a save composition hint tells the user which parts will be sent. On submit useProductUpdateHandler uploads attribute files, sends productUpdate, then productChannelListingUpdate only if the product update succeeded, then variant bulk delete, bulk create and chunked bulk update. Each step's outcome is recorded so a partial failure can be shown as a banner of steps.

nodes.name: Product update view
nodes.summary: Loads a product, its variants grid, categories, collections and tax classes, and connects media, delete and save handlers to the page.
nodes.detail: Runs useProductDetailsQuery and useProductVariantsGrid, registers a refresh callback for the entity, and wires productMediaCreate, productMediaReorder, productMediaBulkDelete and productDelete with notifications. Saving goes through useProductUpdateHandler; reference attributes get their own product, page, category and collection searches.

nodes.name: Product update page
nodes.summary: Lays out the product editor: details, media, attributes, variants grid, availability card, organization, shipping, taxes, setup checklist and save bar.

nodes.name: Product update form state
nodes.summary: Holds every editable value on the product page, including channel listing drafts and variant edits staged across grid pages, and builds the submit payload.
nodes.detail: Uses the shared useForm hooks plus attribute formsets, rich text for the description and a ref holding VariantGridStagedEditsState. Variant removals and generator or manual creates are staged with stageVariantRemovalsInStore and stageVariantCreatesInStore, so they survive pagination; on submit the staged payload and added datagrid rows are merged into variants.stagedCreates. It also reports how many changes are pending for the save bar and the composition hint.

nodes.name: Channel listing drafts
nodes.summary: Keeps the product's per-channel publish, purchase and listing visibility drafts, plus channels added or removed, until save.
nodes.detail: Channel drafts start from the product's saved listings. Channels added in the listings dialog get an empty listing draft; removing a saved channel puts its id in removeChannels, while removing a newly added one just drops its draft. On save the drafts become updateChannels and removeChannels in productChannelListingUpdate, built by getProductChannelsUpdateVariables.

nodes.name: Product save composition
nodes.summary: Summarises what a save will send: details, attributes, dirty channel count and variant edits, creates and deletes, for the hint next to the save bar.
nodes.detail: PRODUCT_DETAILS_SAVE_FIELDS lists the fields that map to productUpdate (name, slug, search engine optimization (SEO) title and description, rating, weight, tax class, category, collections). The same composition pattern is repeated for categories, collections, channels, product types, shipping zones and warehouses.

nodes.name: useProductUpdateHandler()
nodes.summary: Saves the product page by sending up to six kinds of mutations in order and recording each step as success, error or skipped.
nodes.detail: Order: upload new attribute files with fileUpload, send productUpdate (including category so publish validation sees it), then productChannelListingUpdate only when the product update had no errors. Variant removals go in one productVariantBulkDelete, staged creates in one productVariantBulkCreate with errorPolicy REJECT_EVERYTHING so the form can retry all rows, and updates in chunks of 100 rows with REJECT_FAILED_ROWS. Errors are split into product and channel errors for the form; failed steps are kept for the save steps banner. A change to the deprecated rating field is reported to product analytics.
facts: Variant updates are sent in chunks of 100 rows
Bulk create uses errorPolicy REJECT_EVERYTHING; bulk update uses REJECT_FAILED_ROWS
Channel listings are skipped when productUpdate returns errors

nodes.name: getProductChannelsUpdateVariables()
nodes.summary: Builds productChannelListingUpdate input from the channel drafts, keeping only schema fields and forcing purchase on when a purchase date is set.
nodes.detail: Picks channelId, isAvailableForPurchase, availableForPurchaseAt, isPublished, publishedAt and visibleInListings from each draft, so scheduling works the way the server expects: isPublished true with a future publishedAt, and isAvailableForPurchase true with a future availableForPurchaseAt. Only channels that remain after the update and have a draft are sent; removed channels pass through from the form.

nodes.name: Product save steps
nodes.summary: Six named save steps (files, product, channels, variantDelete, variantCreate, variantUpdate), each starting as skipped, with helpers to set and test their status.
nodes.detail: The save handler starts from createInitialProductSaveSteps and marks a step success or error only when that step had work. hasFailedProductSaveStep decides whether the save steps banner is shown, so a partly applied save tells the user which parts went through.

nodes.name: Media and reorder handlers
nodes.summary: Factories for uploading product images one by one, summarising an upload batch, and reordering media and variants with optimistic responses.
nodes.detail: createImageUploadHandler sends productMediaCreate with the file and an empty alt text and throws when the payload has errors, so the gallery can count failures. createImagesUploadCompleteHandler turns success and failure counts into one notice. createImageReorderHandler sends productMediaReorder with an optimistic response so images move at once; createVariantReorderHandler sends productVariantReorder.

nodes.name: Product organization card
nodes.summary: Selects the category, collections and (when not in the header) product type of a product, with paged searches for each.

nodes.name: Product setup and availability diagnostics
nodes.summary: The setup checklist on a new product and the Product Doctor availability card that explains why a product cannot be bought in a channel.
nodes.detail: The setup card turns form drafts and channel diagnostics into a readiness record (channel, category, price, stock, published) and deep-links to the missing step. Product Doctor loads every variant page, runs grouped availability checks per channel, and can verify the result by asking the public GraphQL endpoint without the staff token.

nodes.name: getProductSetupReadiness()
nodes.summary: Pure function that decides whether a product is ready to sell: a shop-ready channel, a category, a priced variant, stock where needed, and a live listing.
nodes.detail: A listed channel is shop-ready when it is active, has at least one warehouse (if the user may see warehouses) and, for shippable products, at least one shipping zone. An offer means some variant has a price in a listed channel. Stock is required only when warehouses are visible and a shop-ready channel exists; it prefers stock in that channel's warehouses. coreReady is true when all of these hold and at least one listing is both published and available for purchase. Missing diagnostics never block.

nodes.name: Product setup checklist
nodes.summary: Checklist card shown on a new product (action=setup) that lists the remaining steps to sell and scrolls to each field; it can be dismissed per product.

nodes.name: Availability card
nodes.summary: Per-channel publish and purchase controls plus diagnostics, including unsaved channel changes and the active stock availability mode.

nodes.name: Availability diagnostics hook
nodes.summary: Combines product, variants and channel setup data into a list of issues per channel that would stop the product from being purchasable.
nodes.detail: Maps the product to diagnostic data, merges channel summaries with the shop's channel diagnostics (warehouses, shipping zones) from the ChannelDiagnostics query, and runs runAvailabilityChecks. Checks are grouped by category (channel, publishing, purchase, stock) at the dispatch site so a new check cannot be miscategorised.

nodes.name: Product Doctor variant loader
nodes.summary: Walks every page of a product's variants for the checks and fails closed on a missing product, stalled pagination or the 50 page cap.

nodes.name: fetchPublicApiProductCheck()
nodes.summary: Asks the GraphQL endpoint for the product per channel with no token or cookies, to see what a storefront would see, paging variants 100 at a time.
nodes.detail: fetchUnauthenticated posts the PublicApiProductCheck query with fetch, credentials omit and no Authorization header. A missing product on the first page means it is not visible in that channel; a product that disappears on a later page, an error, or more than 50 pages throws, so a partial variant list is never reported as verified. The hook runs this for each channel and keeps per-channel status and the time of the last check.
facts: Request uses credentials: omit and no Authorization header

nodes.name: Variants
nodes.summary: The variants datagrid on the product page, the bulk variant generator, and the variant detail and create pages with prices, stock and media.
nodes.detail: On the product page variants are edited in a paginated datagrid; edits, removals and new rows are staged in the form and saved by the product save sequence. The generator builds every combination of chosen selection attribute values, skips existing ones and stages them as bulk create inputs. The variant page edits one variant: attributes, per-channel prices, stock per warehouse, media and checkout limits, saved with a VariantUpdate document that changes stocks and the variant in one request.

nodes.name: Variants datagrid
nodes.summary: Datagrid of a product's variants with name, stock keeping unit (SKU), attributes, channel availability and prices, and stock per warehouse, plus selection, delete and generator entry.
nodes.detail: Stock keeping unit (SKU) cells and price cells are editable inline. Selected variants are tracked by id across pages; new rows are page-local. Removals and generator output are passed up as onStageVariantRemovals and onStageVariantCreates, so nothing is sent until the product is saved.

nodes.name: Variants grid pagination
nodes.summary: Loads one page of a product's variants with the ProductVariantsGrid query, with debounced search, cursor paging and a range label such as 1 to 5 of 16.
nodes.detail: Uses local pagination state and PRODUCT_VARIANTS_PAGINATE_BY from the shared config. The product page uses it instead of the deprecated unbounded Product.variants list.

nodes.name: Staged variant edits
nodes.summary: Keeps variant grid edits keyed by variant id (snapshots, removals, column updates and creates) so they survive moving between grid pages until save.
nodes.detail: syncVariantGridStagedEditsFromPage folds the current page's datagrid changes into the store; rehydrateVariantGridDatagridOpts rebuilds a page's changes when the user comes back; buildVariantGridSubmitPayload produces the removed ids, staged updates and creates the save handler sends. dedupeBulkCreateInputs drops creates with duplicate attribute combinations.

nodes.name: Variant generator dialog
nodes.summary: Dialog to pick values per selection attribute, set optional stock keeping unit (SKU) prefix and starting stock, preview the combinations, and stage the new variants.

nodes.name: toBulkCreateInputs()
nodes.summary: Turns selected attribute values into productVariantBulkCreate inputs: one per new combination, with a name, optional stock keeping unit (SKU) and optional stock per warehouse.
nodes.detail: cartesianProduct builds the combinations and stops at 1,000 to keep the browser responsive, reporting truncation. Combinations that already exist (on the server or staged) are filtered out. The name joins value names with a slash; the stock keeping unit (SKU) joins the prefix with value slugs by hyphens when enabled; stock is added to every listed warehouse only for a valid non-negative number. Non-selection attribute defaults are added with the input field that matches each attribute's type.

nodes.name: Existing variants loader
nodes.summary: Loads all existing variants of a product for the generator, up to 50 pages, so already-made combinations are marked as existing.

nodes.name: Variant detail view
nodes.summary: Loads one variant and saves its attributes, stocks, prices per channel, media assignment and metadata; also deletes and reorders variants.
nodes.detail: Uses useProductVariantDetailsQuery, uploads attribute files first, then sends VariantUpdate, which in one document deletes, creates and updates stocks and updates the variant. Channel price changes go through useSubmitChannels, which calls productChannelListingUpdate and productVariantChannelListingUpdate. Media are assigned or unassigned one at a time.

nodes.name: Variant create view
nodes.summary: Creates one variant with productVariantCreate, then sets its channel prices, metadata and position among the product's variants.
nodes.detail: After productVariantCreate succeeds it sends productVariantChannelListingUpdate for the chosen channel prices, then the metadata mutations; the page's variant switcher can reorder variants with productVariantReorder. Attribute files are uploaded first with fileUpload.

nodes.name: Variant page
nodes.summary: Variant editor layout: variant switcher sidebar, attributes, media, per-channel prices, checkout limits, stocks, shipping weight and metadata.

nodes.name: Variant switcher
nodes.summary: Sidebar list of a product's variants that loads more on scroll, keeps the active one pinned, and supports drag to reorder.

nodes.name: Product media
nodes.summary: The gallery on the product page, image upload with a type check, external media by link, and the single media page for alt text.
nodes.detail: Images are dropped or picked in ProductMedia, filtered by validateProductMediaFiles, and uploaded one request per file with productMediaCreate (multipart upload). External media are added by sending a link as mediaUrl; the server fetches oEmbed data, which parseOembedData reads back for previews. Reordering uses productMediaReorder, and deletion single or bulk mutations.

nodes.name: Product media gallery
nodes.summary: Grid of product images and videos with drag to reorder, multi-select delete and a drop zone for new files.

nodes.name: Media file check
nodes.summary: Accepts files whose type starts with image/ or whose name ends in a known image extension; size is left to the server's MAX_IMAGE_FILE_SIZE.
facts: Accepted extensions: avif, bmp, gif, jpg, jpeg, png, webp

nodes.name: Media detail view
nodes.summary: Edits one media item's alt text and deletes it, using ProductMediaById, productMediaUpdate and productMediaDelete.
nodes.detail: Reads one media item with ProductMediaById, which also returns the sibling media for the navigation strip. Saving sends productMediaUpdate with the alt text; deleting sends productMediaDelete and returns to the product.

nodes.name: External media dialog
nodes.summary: Asks for a media link and submits it as mediaUrl to productMediaCreate; the server resolves the oEmbed data.

nodes.name: Product GraphQL documents
nodes.summary: The queries and mutations the product pages send; GraphQL Code Generator turns them into typed Apollo hooks in the shared graphql folder.
nodes.detail: Documents are gql template literals. The shell's codegen step compiles them into hooks such as useProductCreateMutation, which the views call; every request goes to the single GraphQL endpoint.

nodes.name: Product mutations
nodes.summary: 22 mutation documents for products, variants, stocks, media, channel listings, reordering and export.
nodes.detail: VariantUpdate bundles productVariantStocksDelete, productVariantStocksCreate, productVariantStocksUpdate and productVariantUpdate in one request. ProductVariantBulkCreate and ProductVariantBulkUpdate pass an errorPolicy chosen by the caller.

nodes.name: ProductCreate document
nodes.summary: Mutation document that creates a product and returns its id and errors with attribute details.

nodes.name: ProductUpdate document
nodes.summary: Mutation document that updates a product's fields and attributes by id.

nodes.name: ProductChannelListingUpdate document
nodes.summary: Mutation document that adds, updates and removes a product's channel listings (published, purchasable, visible in listings, dates).

nodes.name: ProductVariantBulkCreate document
nodes.summary: Mutation document that creates many variants of one product in a request, with an error policy.

nodes.name: ProductVariantBulkUpdate document
nodes.summary: Mutation document that updates many variants of one product, including channel listings and stocks, with an error policy.

nodes.name: Product queries
nodes.summary: Query documents for the product list and count, product and variant details, variant pages, grid attribute columns, channel diagnostics and stock keeping unit (SKU) checks.
nodes.detail: ProductList takes both filter and where inputs plus flags that include categories and collections only when needed. ProductVariantsGrid, ProductDoctorVariants and ProductVariantSiblings page through variants with first and after. StockVisibilityMode and ChannelDiagnostics feed Product Doctor.

nodes.name: Product feature announcements
nodes.summary: Six announcement entries (ripples) for new product features such as the availability diagnostics and the variant generator, each with a lifetime and date.

nodes.name: Order discount providers
nodes.summary: React context providers for adding, updating and removing order and order line discounts; they live under products but are used by the order pages.
nodes.detail: OrderDiscountProvider wraps orderDiscountAdd, orderDiscountUpdate and orderDiscountDelete hooks with notifications and dialog state; OrderLineDiscountProvider does the same for line discounts. Their consumers are the order details, draft and summary components owned by the orders area.

nodes.name: Categories
nodes.summary: The category tree list with lazy-loaded children, and the category page with subcategories, products, background image and search engine optimization (SEO) fields.
nodes.detail: The list shows root categories and expands children on demand: each expanded parent loads its children 50 at a time, first from the Apollo cache, then from the network. Expanded ids are remembered in local storage. The category page edits general fields and search engine optimization (SEO) text with categoryUpdate, creates subcategories in a dialog and lists the category's products.

nodes.name: Category list view
nodes.summary: Runs RootCategories with sort and filters, keeps expanded ids in local storage, and wires create and bulk delete.
nodes.detail: Composes three controllers: tree (expand and load children), selection (rows across levels) and bulk delete (categoryBulkDelete then refetch). The expanded ids key is categoryListExpandedIds:v1.

nodes.name: Category tree controller
nodes.summary: Expands and collapses category rows and loads each parent's children page by page, reading the Apollo cache before going to the network.
nodes.detail: Keeps expanded, loading and loaded id sets and a children-by-parent map, and restores the stored expanded ids once on load. Children are flattened into rows with an indent level by categoryTree.ts.

nodes.name: Category children loader
nodes.summary: Reads or fetches one page of a category's children (50 per page) with the CategoryChildren query, network-only on fetch.
nodes.detail: readCategoryChildrenPageFromCache calls readQuery on the Apollo cache and returns null on a miss; fetchCategoryChildrenPage runs the same CategoryChildren query network-only. Both return the children with hasNextPage and endCursor so the tree can show a load more row.

nodes.name: Category details view
nodes.summary: Loads a category with its subcategories and products and wires update, delete, background image removal, subcategory create and bulk delete.
nodes.detail: Runs CategoryDetails with separate local pagination for subcategories and products, registers a refresh callback, and handles background image upload through the shared hook. Saving sends categoryUpdate with name, slug, description, search engine optimization (SEO) fields and background image alt; subcategories are created with categoryCreate under this parent and removed with categoryBulkDelete.

nodes.name: Category GraphQL documents
nodes.summary: Mutation documents to create, update, delete and bulk delete categories.
nodes.detail: Mutations: Mutation documents to create, update, delete and bulk delete categories. Queries (queries.ts): Query documents for root categories, category details with products and subcategories, and one page of children. GraphQL Code Generator compiles both files into typed Apollo hooks in the shared graphql folder, which the views call; every request goes to the one GraphQL endpoint.

nodes.name: Collections
nodes.summary: Collection list, collection page with channel availability and an ordered product list that can be reordered by dragging.
nodes.detail: The collection page saves general fields with collectionUpdate and per-channel publication with collectionChannelListingUpdate. Products are assigned in a dialog that sends collectionAddProducts and collectionReorderProducts in one document; drag and drop sends collectionReorderProducts with an optimistic response so the row moves at once.

nodes.name: Collection list view
nodes.summary: Runs CollectionList for the selected channel and filters, and wires create and bulk delete.
nodes.detail: Builds filter variables from the conditional filter container and the selected channel, runs CollectionList with cursor pagination, and creates a collection from a name-only dialog with collectionCreate.

nodes.name: Collection details view
nodes.summary: Loads a collection and saves its fields, metadata and channel listings; deletes it or its background image.
nodes.detail: Saving sends collectionUpdate for fields and background image, collectionChannelListingUpdate for added, changed and removed channels, and the metadata mutations. Deleting sends collectionDelete and returns to the list.

nodes.name: Collection availability card
nodes.summary: Per-channel published state and publication date for a collection, with channels added or removed through a dialog.

nodes.name: Collection products table
nodes.summary: Paginated, draggable table of the products in a collection, with assign and unassign actions.

nodes.name: Collection product reorder
nodes.summary: Sends collectionReorderProducts for a dropped product with an optimistic response, then shows a success notice.
nodes.detail: The move is sent as one MoveProductInput with sortOrder set to the negated drag shift. The success notice is shown after the await without checking the payload errors.

nodes.name: Collection GraphQL documents
nodes.summary: Mutation documents to create, update, delete and bulk delete collections, assign, unassign and reorder products, and update channel listings.
nodes.detail: Mutations: Mutation documents to create, update, delete and bulk delete collections, assign, unassign and reorder products, and update channel listings. Queries (queries.ts): Query documents for the collection list, collection details and the collection's product page. GraphQL Code Generator compiles both files into typed Apollo hooks in the shared graphql folder, which the views call; every request goes to the one GraphQL endpoint.

nodes.name: Attributes
nodes.summary: Attribute list with type tabs, attribute create and detail pages with values, and the shared helpers that turn attribute form values into GraphQL input.
nodes.detail: Attributes belong to product types, page (model) types or customer types; the list groups them by the type they are assigned to and counts per tab. The detail page edits properties, input type, numeric units, reference targets and values, including pasted value lists and colour or image swatches. attributes/utils is shared by products, variants and pages: prepareAttributesInput builds the attributes input for productUpdate, pageUpdate and variant mutations, and handleUploadMultipleFiles uploads file attribute values first.

nodes.name: Attribute list view
nodes.summary: Lists attributes with filters and type tabs, with counts of attributes per product or page type, and bulk deletes or unassigns them.
nodes.detail: Runs AttributeList plus PageTypeListWithAssignedAttributeCounts and ProductTypeListWithAssignedAttributeCounts for the tab counts. Unassigning from a type uses productAttributeUnassign or pageAttributeUnassign; deleting uses attributeBulkDelete.

nodes.name: Attribute details view
nodes.summary: Loads an attribute with paged values and saves properties, values (create, update, delete, bulk delete, reorder) and metadata.
nodes.detail: Runs AttributeDetails with paginated values and the page and product type counts of where the attribute is used. Values are created, updated, deleted, bulk deleted and reordered with their own mutations as soon as the user acts; the attribute itself is saved with attributeUpdate and the metadata mutations.

nodes.name: Attribute create view
nodes.summary: Creates an attribute with its first values in one attributeCreate call, then writes metadata.
nodes.detail: Values added before the first save are kept locally by useAttributeCreateValues and sent inside attributeCreate as the values list; after creation the view navigates to the attribute page.

nodes.name: Pasted value parser
nodes.summary: Splits clipboard text into attribute values on commas, semicolons, tabs and new lines, but not spaces, so multi-word names stay whole.

nodes.name: Attribute form handlers
nodes.summary: Change handlers for attribute formsets on products, variants and pages, file uploads, reference searches and the conversion to GraphQL input.
nodes.detail: Shared by the products, modeling and variant pages. handleUploadMultipleFiles sends one fileUpload per new file in parallel and the results are merged back before the entity mutation.

nodes.name: prepareAttributesInput()
nodes.summary: Converts attribute form values into AttributeValueInput rows, skipping unchanged optional attributes and choosing the field that matches each input type.
nodes.detail: Compares each value with the previous one and leaves unchanged, non-required attributes out. Files send file (null when cleared, since an omitted attribute is left untouched by the server); plain and rich text, references, single reference, date, date time, swatch, numeric and dropdown each use their own field, and anything else sends values.

nodes.name: Attribute data helpers
nodes.summary: Maps attribute fragments to form data and back, merges file upload results, and resolves reference attribute display data and entity types.
nodes.detail: Holds the lists of input types with dedicated values, reference types and entity types restricted by type, plus getAttributeData used when creating attributes from product types.

nodes.name: Assigned type attributes
nodes.summary: Loads the attributes assigned to a product type or page type for the list's per-type tab, through two type-specific queries.
nodes.detail: Runs ProductTypeAssignedAttributesForList or PageTypeAssignedAttributesForList depending on the tab's type, skipping the other, and returns the merged attribute rows with refetch.

nodes.name: Attribute GraphQL documents
nodes.summary: Mutation documents to create, update, delete and bulk delete attributes, and to create, update, delete, bulk delete and reorder their values.
nodes.detail: Mutations: Mutation documents to create, update, delete and bulk delete attributes, and to create, update, delete, bulk delete and reorder their values. Queries (queries.ts): Query documents for attribute details and list, and product and page types with assigned attribute counts. GraphQL Code Generator compiles both files into typed Apollo hooks in the shared graphql folder, which the views call; every request goes to the one GraphQL endpoint.

nodes.name: Product types
nodes.summary: Product type list and editor: product and variant attributes, which variant attributes drive selection, shipping, tax class and a product page preview.
nodes.detail: Creating a type asks only for a name and kind (regular product or gift card) in a dialog. The editor assigns, unassigns and reorders product and variant attributes, marks variant selection attributes with productAttributeAssignmentUpdate, and can create a new attribute and assign it in one step. A schematic shows how the type's attributes will appear on a product page.

nodes.name: Product type list view
nodes.summary: Lists product types with filters and sort, and wires create and bulk delete.
nodes.detail: Runs ProductTypeList with filters, sort and cursor pagination; bulk delete goes through productTypeBulkDelete after a dialog that shows how many products use the selected types, with a link to view them.

nodes.name: Product type editor view
nodes.summary: Loads a product type and saves its fields, attribute assignments, variant selection, order and metadata, and creates attributes in place.
nodes.detail: Save sends productTypeUpdate, then productAttributeAssignmentUpdate for variant selection changes, then metadata. Attribute dialogs use useProductTypeOperations for assign, unassign, reorder and delete.

nodes.name: executeProductTypeAttributeCreate()
nodes.summary: Creates an attribute from the dialog with attributeCreate and immediately assigns it to the product type as a product or variant attribute.
nodes.detail: If the create fails its errors are returned; if it succeeds but assignment fails, the error message is returned and the attribute stays created but unassigned.

nodes.name: Create product type hook
nodes.summary: Creates a product type from the dialog (name, and regular or gift card kind) with productTypeCreate and opens it; also used from the product list.
nodes.detail: Sends productTypeCreate with the name and the chosen kind (regular or gift card), hasVariants false, and isShippingRequired false only for gift cards, then opens the new type. The product list's create dialog uses the same hook when no suitable type exists.

nodes.name: Product page schematic
nodes.summary: Miniature product page drawn from the type: selection attributes as pickers, other variant attributes as badges, product attributes as details.

nodes.name: Product type GraphQL documents
nodes.summary: Mutation documents to create, update, delete and bulk delete product types, assign, unassign and reorder attributes and set variant selection.
nodes.detail: Mutations: Mutation documents to create, update, delete and bulk delete product types, assign, unassign and reorder attributes and set variant selection. Queries (queries.ts): Query documents for the product type list and product type details. GraphQL Code Generator compiles both files into typed Apollo hooks in the shared graphql folder, which the views call; every request goes to the one GraphQL endpoint.

nodes.name: Content models and model types
nodes.summary: Structured content: models (Saleor pages) built from model types (page types) and their attributes, with list tabs per type.
nodes.detail: The modeling folder is the user-facing name for pages: a model has a title, rich text content, attributes from its model type and a publication state. modelTypes edits page types and their attribute assignments. The model list groups type tabs by a separator in the type name (for example a dash or colon) so many types stay readable.

nodes.name: Model list view
nodes.summary: Lists models with filters and per-type tabs and counts, and wires bulk publish and bulk delete.
nodes.detail: Runs PageList with filters, sort and the selected type tab; tab counts come from usePageTypeTabCounts. Bulk publish and unpublish send pageBulkPublish, bulk delete sends pageBulkDelete.

nodes.name: Model type tab grouping
nodes.summary: Groups model type tabs by a prefix before a separator in the type name; the default separators are an em dash character, a colon and a hyphen.

nodes.name: Model details view
nodes.summary: Loads a model and saves title, content, attributes (after uploading files), publication and metadata with pageUpdate; deletes it.
nodes.detail: On save it uploads new attribute files with handleUploadMultipleFiles, builds attributes with prepareAttributesInput, and sends pageUpdate with title, slug, content, search engine optimization (SEO) fields, publication and attributes, then the metadata mutations.

nodes.name: Model create view
nodes.summary: Creates a model of the chosen type with pageCreate, uploading attribute files first, then writes metadata.
nodes.detail: The page type is picked in a dialog before the page opens. Saving uploads attribute files, sends pageCreate with the type and attributes, writes metadata and navigates to the new model.

nodes.name: Model type editor view
nodes.summary: Loads a page type and saves its name, attribute assignments, attribute order and metadata; deletes it.
nodes.detail: Saving sends pageTypeUpdate and metadata. Attributes are assigned with pageAttributeAssign, unassigned with pageAttributeUnassign and reordered with pageTypeReorderAttributes as the user acts; an attribute can also be created and assigned in place.

nodes.name: Model type list view
nodes.summary: Lists page types with sort and filters, and wires create and bulk delete.
nodes.detail: Runs PageTypeList with filters and sort; creating uses a name-only dialog with pageTypeCreate, and the delete dialog shows how many models use the selected types (PageCount query).

nodes.name: Model GraphQL documents
nodes.summary: Mutation documents to create, update, delete, bulk publish and bulk delete models (pages).
nodes.detail: Mutations: Mutation documents to create, update, delete, bulk publish and bulk delete models (pages). Queries (queries.ts): Query documents for the model list and count, model details, a page type and models of a type. GraphQL Code Generator compiles both files into typed Apollo hooks in the shared graphql folder, which the views call; every request goes to the one GraphQL endpoint.

nodes.name: Model type GraphQL documents
nodes.summary: Mutation documents to create, update, delete and bulk delete page types and assign, unassign and reorder their attributes.
nodes.detail: Mutations: Mutation documents to create, update, delete and bulk delete page types and assign, unassign and reorder their attributes. Queries (queries.ts): Query documents for the page type list and page type details. GraphQL Code Generator compiles both files into typed Apollo hooks in the shared graphql folder, which the views call; every request goes to the one GraphQL endpoint.

nodes.name: Navigation menus
nodes.summary: Menu list and the menu editor: a drag and drop tree of items that link to categories, collections, models or web addresses.
nodes.detail: The menu editor keeps the item tree locally. Dragging items computes move operations, and saving sends one MenuUpdate document with the name change, menuItemMove for every move and menuItemBulkDelete for removed items. Items are created and edited in a dialog whose link can point at a category, collection, page or plain link.

nodes.name: Menu editor view
nodes.summary: Loads a menu with its item tree and saves name, moves and removals with MenuUpdate; creates and edits items with their own mutations.
nodes.detail: The page reports moves and removed item ids on save; the view sends one MenuUpdate document carrying menuUpdate for the name, menuItemMove with every move and menuItemBulkDelete for removed ids, then refetches. Item dialogs call menuItemCreate and menuItemUpdate directly.

nodes.name: Menu tree operations
nodes.summary: Finds, removes and inserts menu items by path in the nested tree, used to apply drag moves locally before save.
nodes.detail: findNode returns the index path of an item, getNode reads it, and removal and insertion rebuild the nested arrays immutably, so the editor can show the result of a drag before saving.

nodes.name: Sortable menu tree
nodes.summary: Menu items rendered in the shared SortableTree component (built on dnd-kit), each mapped to its type and link for display.

nodes.name: Menu item dialog
nodes.summary: Creates or edits a menu item: name and a link to a category, collection, page or web address, validated with a schema.

nodes.name: Menu list view
nodes.summary: Lists menus and wires create, delete and bulk delete.
nodes.detail: Runs MenuList with sort and pagination; create opens a name dialog with menuCreate and navigates to the new menu; delete and bulk delete use menuDelete and menuBulkDelete.

nodes.name: Menu GraphQL documents
nodes.summary: Mutation documents to create, update, delete and bulk delete menus and to create, update, move and bulk delete menu items.
nodes.detail: Mutations: Mutation documents to create, update, delete and bulk delete menus and to create, update, move and bulk delete menu items. Queries (queries.ts): Query documents for the menu list and a menu with its item tree. GraphQL Code Generator compiles both files into typed Apollo hooks in the shared graphql folder, which the views call; every request goes to the one GraphQL endpoint.

nodes.name: Translations
nodes.summary: Language list, entity lists per kind, and side-by-side editors that translate products, variants, media, categories, collections, models, discounts, attributes, shipping methods and menu items.
nodes.detail: A language is picked first (the last used one is remembered), then an entity kind and an entity. Detail pages show source and translation per field with progress; edits to several fields are saved together. Entity fields go in one translate mutation for that entity, and attribute values are saved one mutation per value. The product translation form also sends a form payload to an active app extension and can apply the values the app returns.

nodes.name: Language list view
nodes.summary: Lists the shop's languages from the shop context; the translations router reopens the last used language from a local cache stack.
nodes.detail: A thin view: it passes shop.languages to the list page. Remembering the last language is done by the router with useRememberLastTranslationLocale and the CachedLocalesStack kept in local storage.

nodes.name: Translatable entity lists
nodes.summary: Tabs per entity kind with a paginated list of entities and their translation progress for the chosen language.
nodes.detail: Reads the entity kind from the address, renders the matching list view (products, categories, collections, models, vouchers, sales, attributes, shipping methods or menu items) with shared query variables for paging and filtering.

nodes.name: Product translation view
nodes.summary: Loads a product's translation details and saves entity fields with productTranslate and attribute values with attributeValueTranslate.
nodes.detail: Passes the ProductTranslationDetails query and the productTranslate and attributeValueTranslate mutations to the product translation page, which uses the shared entity view hook.

nodes.name: Translation entity view hook
nodes.summary: Shared logic for every translation detail view: query, language pair, save state and feedback, and bulk submit of dirty fields.
nodes.detail: Takes the details query, the entity mutation and an optional attribute value mutation. It resolves the source and target language pair, tracks which field is being edited and saved, and on save calls submitBulkTranslations, which sends entity fields in one mutation and then attribute values one by one. Errors map back to fields.

nodes.name: Bulk translation submit
nodes.summary: Saves all dirty entity fields in one mutation and attribute values one by one, and maps returned errors back to fields.
nodes.detail: submitBulkEntityTranslations merges all dirty entity fields into one input and calls the entity mutation once. submitBulkAttributeValueTranslations calls the attribute value mutation once per field, in sequence. Both map mutation errors to field names with a fallback message.

nodes.name: Translation progress
nodes.summary: Counts translated fields and flags blank translations stored as empty strings or empty rich text documents, which storefronts show as blank.
nodes.detail: isFieldTranslationComplete counts a field as done when it has a non-blank translation. A blank stored instead of null only counts when the field accepts null, the original has content and no app draft would be saved instead.

nodes.name: App translation bridge
nodes.summary: Sends the product translation form to an active app extension as a product-translate payload and applies the field values the app sends back.
nodes.detail: createProductTranslateFormPayloadEvent packs the product name, description and search engine optimization (SEO) fields with original, current and translated values. The hook reads the active app extension from the extensions context and, when the app answers with new values, writes them into the cached form fields.

nodes.name: Translation GraphQL documents
nodes.summary: Mutation documents to translate products, variants, media, categories, collections, pages, vouchers, sales, attributes, attribute values, shipping methods and menu items.
nodes.detail: Mutations: Mutation documents to translate products, variants, media, categories, collections, pages, vouchers, sales, attributes, attribute values, shipping methods and menu items. Queries (queries.ts): Query documents for translatable entity lists and the translation details of each entity kind. GraphQL Code Generator compiles both files into typed Apollo hooks in the shared graphql folder, which the views call; every request goes to the one GraphQL endpoint.

nodes.name: Configuration hub
nodes.summary: The Configuration page: a permission-filtered menu of settings sections and a fuzzy search over a catalog of individual settings that deep-links to each control.
nodes.detail: createConfigurationMenu returns sections (store attributes, product settings, taxes, shipping, users and permissions, and so on) whose items carry the permissions needed to open them; items the user lacks are hidden. The settings catalog is a hand-written list of settings per hub (orders, store, refunds, gift cards, notifications, channels) with titles, keywords, breadcrumbs and a stable hash; it is filtered by permissions, translated, and searched with Fuse.js. Picking a result navigates to the page and scrolls to the element whose id equals the hash.

nodes.name: Configuration route
nodes.summary: Renders the Configuration page with the configuration menu, the signed-in user and the dashboard and core version numbers.
nodes.detail: Builds the menu with createConfigurationMenu and passes it, the signed-in user and the dashboard and core versions to ConfigurationPage, which hides items the user lacks permissions for.

nodes.name: Configuration menu
nodes.summary: Builds the configuration sections and items with icons, links and the permissions each item needs, such as MANAGE_CHANNELS for channels and MANAGE_STAFF for staff.
facts: The Taxes item declares no permissions, unlike its siblings

nodes.name: Configuration page
nodes.summary: Lays out the menu sections as navigation cards, hiding items the user lacks permissions for, with the settings search on top.

nodes.name: Settings search box
nodes.summary: Search field with keyboard navigation over the settings catalog; results show breadcrumbs and open the exact setting.

nodes.name: Settings catalog
nodes.summary: Concatenates the per-hub setting entries (orders, store, refunds, gift cards, notifications, channels) into one searchable list.

nodes.name: Catalog permission filter
nodes.summary: Drops catalog entries the user may not open (any or all of their permissions) and translates titles, keywords and breadcrumbs.

nodes.name: searchSettingsCatalog()
nodes.summary: Weighted fuzzy search over the resolved catalog: title first, then keywords, then description and breadcrumbs.

nodes.name: Settings catalog guide
nodes.summary: How to add a setting to the catalog: entry per hub, keyword aliases, a stable hash on the control, permissions and ownership, and the test to run.

nodes.name: Channels
nodes.summary: Channel list and create dialog, the channel page with setup checklist, warehouse and shipping assignment, payment apps, order and checkout settings, and bulk publishing of products.
nodes.detail: A channel is created from a short dialog (name, slug, currency, default country) with operator defaults for stock, payment, order and checkout settings, or as a copy of another channel that starts inactive. The new channel opens with a setup checklist: create or assign warehouses and shipping zones, review payment apps and taxes, publish products, then activate. Saving the channel page sends channelUpdate; before removing warehouses or zones it previews which warehouse to zone links the server would silently drop. Bulk publish walks up to 50 chosen products and, per product, updates the channel listing, then variant prices and stock.

nodes.name: Channel list view
nodes.summary: Lists channels with shipping coverage counts and plan limits, creates or duplicates a channel and opens it in setup mode.
nodes.detail: On create it sends channelCreate with buildChannelCreateInput, refetches the signed-in user, the channel picker and the list, refetches shop limits and navigates to the channel with action=setup. Duplicating loads the source channel's shipping zones first so they can be copied.

nodes.name: Create channel dialog
nodes.summary: Asks for name, slug (checked for availability), currency with suggestions from the country, and default country; also used to duplicate a channel.

nodes.name: buildChannelCreateInput()
nodes.summary: Builds channelCreate input from the dialog plus operator defaults, or copies settings, warehouses and shipping zones from a source channel and starts it inactive.
nodes.detail: The slug falls back to a slugified name and the currency is upper-cased. Defaults come from getChannelCreateDefaults: allocation strategy, transaction flow, release of funds for expired checkouts, order expiry and confirmation, and checkout completion. A duplicate copies those settings and the warehouse and zone assignments, but not the catalog or tax configuration, and sets isActive false so the copy is not live by accident.

nodes.name: Channel details view
nodes.summary: Loads a channel and wires save, activate, deactivate, delete, duplicate, the setup checklist, warehouse and zone dialogs, payment apps and bulk publish.
nodes.detail: Uses useChannelQuery plus shipping zone, warehouse and setup review statistics queries. The save handler sends channelUpdate with warehouse and zone changes and reorders warehouses with channelReorderWarehouses. The page gets a previewChannelUnlinks callback so it can warn before a save that would drop warehouse to zone links. Setup actions come from useChannelSetupActions.

nodes.name: Channel page
nodes.summary: Channel editor with section navigation: general, orders, payments and checkout, inventory (warehouses), delivery (shipping zones), payment apps and a catalog summary.

nodes.name: Channel settings form
nodes.summary: Fields for name, slug, currency, country, stock allocation, mark-as-paid and transaction flow strategies, order expiry, fund release and automatic checkout completion.

nodes.name: Channel setup checklist
nodes.summary: Checklist for a new channel: warehouse, shipping, payment apps, tax status and products, with Activate enabled once warehouse and shipping are in place.

nodes.name: useChannelSetupActions()
nodes.summary: Setup checklist actions: create a warehouse and assign it, create a shipping zone with a priced rate for the channel, or assign existing warehouses and zones.
nodes.detail: Warehouse: createWarehouse once, remembering the created id so a retry after a failed assign updates it instead of creating another, then channelUpdate addWarehouses. Shipping: shippingZoneCreate with the chosen country, this channel and the channel's warehouses, then shippingPriceCreate of type PRICE, then shippingMethodChannelListingUpdate with the price. If the price listing fails the zone and rate are kept and only an error notice is shown. Assignments send channelUpdate with addWarehouses or addShippingZones and refetch the channel queries.

nodes.name: Channel unlink preview
nodes.summary: Before a channel save, lists warehouse and shipping zone pairs that would lose their only shared channel, so the user is warned.
nodes.detail: Reads every page of the channel's shipping zones with ChannelZoneWarehouseLinks (network-only), finds candidate links touched by the removed warehouses or zones, then asks WarehouseSharesChannels for each distinct warehouse and channel set, four at a time, whether another channel still links them.

nodes.name: Payment apps section
nodes.summary: Lists installed apps that handle payments, with links to configure each, for users with MANAGE_APPS.

nodes.name: Channel catalog summary
nodes.summary: Shows how many products are published, unpublished or listed in the channel, with links to the filtered product list and the bulk publish action.

nodes.name: Bulk publish dialog
nodes.summary: Four-step dialog: pick products (search, filter or pasted spreadsheet), set defaults for publish state, price, cost and stock, review per product, confirm.

nodes.name: useBulkPublishToChannelSubmit()
nodes.summary: Publishes chosen products into one channel one by one: channel listing first, then variant prices, cost and stock in chunks, with progress per product.
nodes.detail: Loads the products in one query (at most 50), skips any without a category when publishing, then sends productChannelListingUpdate with the chosen published, visible and purchasable flags. It then reloads all variants (so a retry does not create listings twice) and sends productVariantBulkUpdate in chunks of 100 with REJECT_FAILED_ROWS. Failures are recorded per product and the run is reported to analytics as success, partial success or failure.

nodes.name: Channel GraphQL documents
nodes.summary: Mutation documents to create, update, delete, activate and deactivate channels and reorder their warehouses.
nodes.detail: Mutations: Mutation documents to create, update, delete, activate and deactivate channels and reorder their warehouses. Queries (queries.ts): Query documents for channel lists, one channel by id or slug, shipping coverage, setup review statistics, payment apps and bulk publish data. GraphQL Code Generator compiles both files into typed Apollo hooks in the shared graphql folder, which the views call; every request goes to the one GraphQL endpoint.

nodes.name: Shipping zones and rates
nodes.summary: Shipping zone list, zone editor (countries, channels, warehouses, postal code rules) and price or weight based rates with per-channel prices and excluded products.
nodes.detail: A zone links countries to channels and warehouses; a warehouse can only be linked when it shares a channel with the zone, which the editor checks before showing the picker. Removing a channel from a zone is previewed to list warehouses that would be unlinked. Rates are created with shippingPriceCreate and then priced per channel with shippingMethodChannelListingUpdate; if pricing fails the new rate is deleted again. The country dialog offers European Union and North America presets and a rest of the world option.

nodes.name: Shipping zone list view
nodes.summary: Lists shipping zones, bulk deletes them and changes the shop's default weight unit through shopSettingsUpdate.
nodes.detail: Runs ShippingZones with sort and pagination. Bulk delete sends shippingZoneBulkDelete; the weight unit dialog sends shopSettingsUpdate with defaultWeightUnit through the UpdateDefaultWeightUnit document.

nodes.name: Shipping zone view
nodes.summary: Loads a zone and saves name, countries, channels, warehouses and postal code rules with shippingZoneUpdate; deletes the zone or its rates.
nodes.detail: Runs ShippingZone and the rest of the world countries query. Saving sends shippingZoneUpdate with added and removed countries, channels and warehouses; before removing channels the page asks which warehouses would be unlinked. Rates are deleted with shippingPriceDelete. The create page sends shippingZoneCreate.

nodes.name: Shipping rate view
nodes.summary: Edits a rate's name, type limits, delivery days, per-channel price and order value range, postal codes, taxes and excluded products.
nodes.detail: Saving sends shippingPriceUpdate with postal code rules to add and delete, then shippingMethodChannelListingUpdate for channel prices. Excluded products are added with shippingPriceExcludeProducts and removed with shippingPriceRemoveProductFromExclude.

nodes.name: useShippingRateCreator()
nodes.summary: Creates a price or weight rate, then sets its channel prices; if pricing fails it deletes the new rate so no unpriced rate is left.
nodes.detail: Variables come from getCreateShippingPriceRateVariables or getCreateShippingWeightRateVariables, which parse optional order price and weight limits and add new postal code rules. On success it navigates to the rate page.

nodes.name: Zone warehouse eligibility
nodes.summary: Splits warehouses into those a zone may link (they share one of its channels) and those it may not, treating a failed check as all eligible.
facts: Eligibility queries use first at most 100, the server's maximum
nodes.detail: useZoneWarehouseEligibility queries which of the candidate warehouses share a channel with the zone, at most 100 at a time; resolveEligibleWarehouseIds treats unchecked ids as eligible and a failed check as unknown, so the picker never blocks on errors.

nodes.name: Zone countries dialog
nodes.summary: Picks countries for a zone with search, European Union (27 states) and North America presets, and a rest of the world option.

nodes.name: Shipping GraphQL documents
nodes.summary: Mutation documents for zones (create, update, delete, bulk delete), rates (create, update, delete), rate channel prices, excluded products, and the default weight unit.
nodes.detail: Mutations: Mutation documents for zones (create, update, delete, bulk delete), rates (create, update, delete), rate channel prices, excluded products, and the default weight unit. Queries (queries.ts): Query documents for zone lists and details, zone channels, channel zones, zone and warehouse links, eligibility and counts. GraphQL Code Generator compiles both files into typed Apollo hooks in the shared graphql folder, which the views call; every request goes to the one GraphQL endpoint.

nodes.name: Warehouses
nodes.summary: Warehouse list with sellability status, warehouse page with address, pickup options, channels and shipping zones, and a setup checklist.
nodes.detail: Warehouse to channel and warehouse to zone links are stored on the channel and zone sides, so the warehouse page changes them by sending channelUpdate or shippingZoneUpdate per entity. warehouseChannelMembership batches those into aliased mutations, four per request because the server rejects documents with more mutations than its limit, and reports success per entity. Membership is read with one matrix query when channels times warehouses is at most 5,000, otherwise with per-warehouse probes. Removing a channel warns about zones that would lose their only shared channel.

nodes.name: Warehouse list view
nodes.summary: Lists warehouses with place, pickup, channels and a sellable status, and creates or deletes warehouses.
nodes.detail: Runs WarehouseList with filters and pagination plus the channel membership matrix, so each row can show channels and whether its stock can be sold. Create sends createWarehouse from a dialog; delete sends deleteWarehouse.

nodes.name: Warehouse details view
nodes.summary: Loads a warehouse and saves its address, name, email, privacy and click and collect option with updateWarehouse; deletes it.
nodes.detail: Runs WarehouseDetails and shows a retry state if it fails. Saving sends updateWarehouse with address, name, email, isPrivate and clickAndCollectOption; changing the pickup option also sets privacy, because pickup from stock at this location needs a public warehouse (pickupOptionAfterPrivateChange).

nodes.name: Warehouse channels card logic
nodes.summary: Adds and removes the warehouse's channels, warning first about shipping zones that would be unlinked, and reloads the warehouse after the change.
nodes.detail: Reads which channels hold the warehouse (matrix or probes), adds or removes it through runWarehouseLinkUpdates with channelUpdate, and before removal lists zones that would lose their only shared channel, since the server drops those links without an error. The warehouse is reloaded afterwards.

nodes.name: Warehouse zone assignment
nodes.summary: Assigns or unassigns shipping zones from the warehouse page through batched shippingZoneUpdate calls, with a dialog listing all zones.
nodes.detail: Loads zones that can be assigned, then links or unlinks them with runWarehouseLinkUpdates through shippingZoneUpdate, reporting per zone which changes failed. Needs MANAGE_SHIPPING.

nodes.name: buildWarehouseLinkUpdates()
nodes.summary: Builds one GraphQL document with aliased channelUpdate or shippingZoneUpdate fields, each adding or removing the warehouse on one entity.
nodes.detail: runWarehouseLinkUpdates sends these in chunks of MEMBERSHIP_UPDATE_CHUNK_SIZE (4) with errorPolicy all and returns one success flag per entity; a chunk that fails as a whole marks all its entities failed. buildMembershipProbe does the same for reads, one aliased warehouses count per channel.

nodes.name: Warehouse setup checklist
nodes.summary: Shows a new warehouse's remaining tasks: link it to a channel and to a shipping zone, so its stock can be sold.

nodes.name: Warehouse GraphQL documents
nodes.summary: Mutation documents to create, update and delete warehouses.
nodes.detail: Mutations: Mutation documents to create, update and delete warehouses. Queries (queries.ts): Query documents for warehouse lists and details, counts, stock counts, channel membership matrix, shared channels and zones to assign. GraphQL Code Generator compiles both files into typed Apollo hooks in the shared graphql folder, which the views call; every request goes to the one GraphQL endpoint.

nodes.name: Taxes
nodes.summary: Tax configuration per channel (charge taxes, flat rates or a tax app, gross prices, country exceptions), flat rates per country, and tax classes.
nodes.detail: Three tabs. Channels: one tax configuration per channel; the strategy picker lists installed tax apps by identifier, flat rates, and the legacy Avalara plugin id. Picking an app sends taxCalculationStrategy TAX_APP with taxAppId set to the app identifier; flat rates send FLAT_RATES and a null taxAppId. Countries: flat rates per country and tax class. Classes: tax classes with per-country rates and metadata.

nodes.name: Channel tax view
nodes.summary: Loads tax configurations (first 100 only) and saves the selected one with taxConfigurationUpdate.
nodes.detail: There is no pagination: a shop with more than 100 channels cannot reach the rest from this tab.
facts: useTaxConfigurationsListQuery is called with first: 100 and no paging

nodes.name: Channel tax page
nodes.summary: Form for one channel's tax configuration: charge taxes, strategy (app or flat rates), gross prices, prices entered with tax and country exceptions.

nodes.name: useTaxStrategyChoices()
nodes.summary: Builds the tax strategy options: every available tax app (value is its identifier, with a link to its app page), flat rates, and the legacy plugin:mirumee.taxes.avalara.
nodes.detail: Reads shop.availableTaxApps with the TaxStrategyChoices query. The legacy plugin choice is kept for shops still on the Avalara plugin until they move to the AvaTax app.

nodes.name: Tax strategy mapping
nodes.summary: Maps between the picker value and the server's fields: FLAT_RATES, or TAX_APP with taxAppId; a TAX_APP configuration without taxAppId shows as legacy-flow.
nodes.detail: getTaxAppId returns the picker value for anything except flat rates, so an untouched legacy-flow value is sent as taxAppId legacy-flow on save, which the server's tax app check does not recognise.

nodes.name: Country tax rates view
nodes.summary: Edits flat tax rates per country and tax class with taxCountryConfigurationUpdate and removes a country with taxCountryConfigurationDelete.
nodes.detail: Runs TaxCountriesList and TaxClassesList. Saving a country sends taxCountryConfigurationUpdate with a rate per tax class; removing a country sends taxCountryConfigurationDelete.

nodes.name: Tax classes view
nodes.summary: Creates, renames and deletes tax classes, sets their per-country rates and writes their metadata.
nodes.detail: Runs TaxClassesList and TaxCountriesList. A new class is created with taxClassCreate, edits go through taxClassUpdate with per-country rates, deletes through taxClassDelete, and metadata through the shared metadata mutations.

nodes.name: Tax GraphQL documents
nodes.summary: Mutation documents to update a channel's tax configuration, update or delete country rates, and create, update or delete tax classes.
nodes.detail: Mutations: Mutation documents to update a channel's tax configuration, update or delete country rates, and create, update or delete tax classes. Queries (queries.ts): Query documents for tax configurations, country rates, tax classes, tax class assignment and the available tax apps. GraphQL Code Generator compiles both files into typed Apollo hooks in the shared graphql folder, which the views call; every request goes to the one GraphQL endpoint.

nodes.name: Staff members
nodes.summary: Staff list, invitations, staff member page (status, permission groups, resend invite) and the signed-in user's own profile, avatar and password.
nodes.detail: Inviting sends staffCreate with a redirect address built from the dashboard's new password route, so the server emails a set-password link; the invite dialog preselects the Full Access group when present. Because invited users count as confirmed, a member who has never signed in (lastLogin empty) is shown as a pending invite, and resending uses requestPasswordReset. Editing your own profile uses accountUpdate, userAvatarUpdate, userAvatarDelete and passwordChange.

nodes.name: Staff list view
nodes.summary: Lists staff members with filters, sort, configurable columns and plan limits, and opens the invite dialog.
nodes.detail: Runs StaffList with filters, sort, pagination and plan limits; the invite button opens the shared invite provider so the same dialog works from other pages.

nodes.name: Staff invite hook
nodes.summary: Sends staffCreate for an invite with the chosen permission groups and a set-password redirect, marks the onboarding step done and notifies.
nodes.detail: Sends staffCreate with name, email, permission groups and a redirect address joined from the mount path and the new password route. Field errors such as a duplicate email are shown in the dialog; on success the onboarding step invite-staff is marked done.

nodes.name: Staff member view
nodes.summary: Loads a staff member and saves name, email, active status and permission groups, deletes them, resends the invite, and edits your own profile.
nodes.detail: For another member it saves with staffUpdate (permission groups diffed with groupsDiff) and deletes with staffDelete; a pending invite can be resent with requestPasswordReset. For the signed-in user it uses accountUpdate, userAvatarUpdate, userAvatarDelete and passwordChange instead.

nodes.name: Staff invite status
nodes.summary: Treats an active member with no lastLogin as a pending invite, since invites do not change isConfirmed, and maps status to a label and dot colour.

nodes.name: Staff GraphQL documents
nodes.summary: Mutation documents to invite, update and delete staff, and to update your own account, avatar and password.
nodes.detail: Mutations: Mutation documents to invite, update and delete staff, and to update your own account, avatar and password. Queries (queries.ts): Query documents for the staff list and one staff member's details. GraphQL Code Generator compiles both files into typed Apollo hooks in the shared graphql folder, which the views call; every request goes to the one GraphQL endpoint.

nodes.name: Permission groups
nodes.summary: Permission group list, create page and group page with permissions, channel access restrictions and members.
nodes.detail: A group holds permission codes, optional restriction to some channels, and staff members. The group page computes differences against the saved state (permissions, users, channels) and sends one permissionGroupUpdate with add and remove lists. Helpers stop a user from granting more permissions or channels than they hold themselves.

nodes.name: Permission group view
nodes.summary: Loads a group and saves permission, member and channel changes in one permissionGroupUpdate; deletes the group; assigns and unassigns members in dialogs.
nodes.detail: Diffs permissions, members and channels against the loaded group and sends permissionGroupUpdate with add and remove lists and restrictedAccessToChannels. Deleting sends permissionGroupDelete; errors about members are shown in a dialog.

nodes.name: Permission group create view
nodes.summary: Creates a group with name, permissions and channel restriction using permissionGroupCreate.
nodes.detail: Sends permissionGroupCreate with the name, chosen permission codes, restricted channels flag and channel ids, then opens the new group.

nodes.name: Permission group list view
nodes.summary: Lists permission groups with sort and deletes them.
nodes.detail: Runs PermissionGroupList with sort and pagination and deletes a group with permissionGroupDelete from a confirmation dialog.

nodes.name: Permission group diffs
nodes.summary: Computes added and removed permissions, users and channels against the saved group, and checks the user does not exceed their own permissions or channels.
nodes.detail: permissionsDiff, usersDiff and channelsDiff compare form and saved values and return add and remove lists. arePermissionsExceeded and the channel helpers keep users from granting more than they hold.

nodes.name: Permission group GraphQL documents
nodes.summary: Mutation documents to create, update and delete permission groups.

nodes.name: Store details and notifications
nodes.summary: Store details (name, address, store metadata) and the notifications settings: staff email templates over the admin email plugin, order alert recipients and links to customer email apps.
nodes.detail: Site settings send shopSettingsUpdate and shopAddressUpdate in one document. Staff emails are the admin email plugin's global configuration: per-notification subject and template mode (default, custom, off) plus Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) fields, saved with pluginUpdate; SMTP connection errors returned by the server are mapped onto the form fields. Order alert recipients are staff or plain addresses kept with staffNotificationRecipientCreate and Delete. Customer emails are handled by an app; the old customer route redirects to it.

nodes.name: Store details view
nodes.summary: Loads shop settings and saves store name, description and company address with shopSettingsUpdate and shopAddressUpdate in one request; shop metadata has its own dialog.
nodes.detail: Runs SiteSettings and saves with one ShopSettingsUpdate document that carries shopSettingsUpdate and shopAddressUpdate, so name, description and company address are saved together.

nodes.name: Notifications hub

nodes.name: Staff emails view
nodes.summary: Edits the admin email plugin's global configuration: on or off, per-notification subject and template, and Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) host, port, sender and security.
nodes.detail: Reads the plugin mirumee.notifications.admin_email with the Plugin query, turns its configuration items into form state with emailNotificationConfig, and saves the changed items with pluginUpdate. Can export the templates and switch delivery back to the default.

nodes.summary: Plugin ids for admin and legacy user emails, app identifiers for the Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP), customer emails and product feed apps, hosted app manifest addresses and SMTP field names.

flows.name: A product is created and made available in a channel
flows.summary: From the create dialog on the product list to a product that is published, purchasable and verified in one channel.

steps.text: A staff member opens Products and chooses Create product. The list view opens the create dialog through the action=create-product address.
The dialog searches product types and asks for a name. Choosing a type also tells the dashboard whether the type has variants.
productCreate is sent with only name and type. For a simple type a default variant is created too; if that fails the product is deleted again.
The server creates the product and returns its id. The dashboard marks the onboarding step done and opens the product with the setup checklist.
The setup card checks what is still missing to sell: a shop-ready channel, a category, a priced variant, stock in that channel's warehouses, and a live listing.
The staff member adds the channel, sets it published and available for purchase, picks a category and enters a price. All of this stays in the form until Save.
Save sends productUpdate first (so the category is stored), then productChannelListingUpdate, then the variant creates and updates with prices and stock.
The server stores the product's listing in the channel with its publish and purchase flags and dates.

On the availability card the staff member can verify the result: the dashboard asks the GraphQL endpoint for the product without its token, as a storefront would, and reports whether it is visible and in stock.

flows.name: A channel is set up with warehouses and shipping
flows.summary: From creating a channel to an active channel with a warehouse, a priced shipping rate and published products.

steps.text: On Channels the staff member chooses Add channel, or duplicates an existing one.
The dialog asks for name, slug (checked for availability), currency and default country.
The input adds operator defaults for stock allocation, payments, orders and checkout. A duplicate copies settings, warehouses and zones and starts inactive.
The server creates the channel. The dashboard refreshes the user's channels and opens the channel with action=setup.
The setup checklist lists warehouse, shipping, payment apps, taxes and products. Activate stays disabled until a warehouse and shipping exist.

Create warehouse sends createWarehouse and then channelUpdate with addWarehouses. Create shipping sends shippingZoneCreate for one country with this channel and its warehouses, shippingPriceCreate, and shippingMethodChannelListingUpdate with the price.
The server creates the zone already linked to the channel and the channel's warehouses.
From the catalog section the staff member bulk publishes up to 50 products: each gets a channel listing, then variant prices and stock in the channel's warehouses.
Finally Activate sends channelActivate. Later edits to warehouses and zones are previewed for links the server would drop.

flows.name: A channel's taxes are handed to a tax app
flows.summary: How choosing a tax app on the Taxes page becomes a taxAppId the API validates.

steps.text: Taxes, Channels tab: the view loads the tax configurations (first 100) and selects one channel.
The strategy picker lists every available tax app by identifier, flat rates, and the legacy Avalara plugin id.
On save the choice becomes taxCalculationStrategy TAX_APP with taxAppId set to the app identifier, or FLAT_RATES with no app.
The server checks that the taxAppId belongs to an active tax app or an active plugin and stores the configuration; checkout tax calculation then calls that app.
With the AvaTax app chosen, the channel's checkouts and orders are taxed by its synchronous webhooks.
